description: The line plot illustrates the performance of different methods for multivariate anomaly detection, measured by the Area Under the Curve (AUC) in percent, as a function of the parameter N, which ranges from 0 to 20 on a linear scale. The y-axis represents AUC (%) and spans from 75% to 100%, with major tick marks at 5% intervals. Five distinct methods are plotted, each represented by a unique combination of color, marker, and line style: a blue line with circle markers starts at approximately 94% AUC when N=0, rises to 98% at N=5, remains flat until N=10, then declines to 94% at N=20; a red line with square markers begins at 87%, increases to 98% at N=10, then drops to 91% at N=20; an orange line with diamond markers starts at 84%, rises steadily to 95% at N=10, and plateaus near 94% through N=20; a green line with star markers begins at 86%, climbs to 94% at N=10, and continues to 92% at N=20; and a purple line with triangle markers remains nearly flat at 79% from N=0 to N=5, spikes to 97% at N=10, then declines to 82% at N=20. The plot suggests varying sensitivity to the parameter N across methods, with most achieving peak performance around N=10.
